title: VTC in mimid: carry the SDP in the call room, which authenticates it and makes the 1:1 demo need no media key
description:
From reading MarkAtwood/ParlorVTC on 2026-11-23 at Mark's suggestion.
Parlor is a 1:1 asymmetric voice queue: two HTML files, no server, no
build step, ~1100 lines of ES modules, WebRTC P2P voice, and signalling
over public Nostr relays.

THE IDEA WORTH TAKING. Parlor carries the WebRTC offer, answer and ICE
candidates inside NIP-04 encrypted direct messages (NIP-PARLOR.md
"Queue and Signaling Messages (kind:4)"): the relay carries signalling it
cannot read, and the media never touches it. The analogue for mimid is
exact and better: carry the SDP as MIMI messages IN THE CALL ROOM. The
call room stops being only a key source and becomes the signalling
channel, which it is already suited to -- E2EE, ordered by the hub,
fanned out to exactly the call's members and nobody else.

WHAT MIMI GETS THAT PARLOR CANNOT HAVE. Parlor's SPEC §Authentication
says "All Nostr events are signed with sender's Ed25519 key... No
additional authentication layer needed", but a supplicant's key is
ephemeral and generated per session, and §Impersonation concedes
"Supplicants are anonymous by design". So the host cannot know who
called. In MIMI the SDP travels inside the MLS group, so THE DTLS
FINGERPRINTS IN IT ARE AUTHENTICATED BY MLS, bound to the sender's
credential identity. No short authentication string, no reading a
fingerprint aloud. draft-atwood-jmap-vtc's e2eeFingerprint field and
jmap-vtc-e2ee-guide.md §8 "Fingerprint verification" are both
unnecessary for a MIMI-backed call, because MLS has already done it.
That is a demonstrable advantage and belongs in the draft.

AND IT REORDERS THE BUILD. WebRTC peer-to-peer is DTLS-SRTP, which is
already end-to-end encrypted between two peers. So a 1:1 call needs NO
media_secret, NO SFrame and NO SFU: SDP over MIMI messages plus WebRTC is
a working, authenticated, end-to-end encrypted call. media_secret is
needed when media passes through an SFU, which is the GROUP case.

That means the shortest path to the demo is SIGNALLING, not keying, and
we built keying first (bead mimid-1wgh.108). Not wasted -- it is what
makes the group case work and it is what draft-atwood-mimi-calls is
about -- but the 1:1 demo is reachable sooner than the build order on
decision mimid-1wgh.113 implies.

WHERE THE SDP GOES, and it is spec-correct rather than a repurposing.
mimi-content-10 §5.10: "a description of a multimedia session, or a URI
used to join one". Everything so far has used the SECOND half, the join
URI (bead mimid-1wgh.114.3). The FIRST half is the slot for SDP, and
nobody has used it. mimid already anticipates it and declines: our
content.rs says "Any other inline session description (SDP, say) is left
out", and draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 §Calls says such a part "maps to
no MessageAction, because JMAP Chat has no field for one". So the
container exists, we already parse around it, and using it is the
opposite of the mimi:// mistake of bead mimid-1wgh.114.1.

THE PART THAT CANNOT BE PEER-TO-PEER: TURN. Parlor hardcodes Jami's
public servers with the credentials ring/ring, and its SPEC is straight
about the consequence -- "TURN servers know: IP addresses of call
participants, that encrypted bytes are flowing". For mimid that is a
deployment configuration item and a Security Considerations line, and it
is the one third party no amount of MLS removes.

SHAPE WORTH COPYING: no build step, no dependencies, no npm, runs from
file://. A mimid demo client could be the same -- a static page speaking
JMAP to the local agent and WebRTC to the peer. That does not breach
decision mimid-1wgh.38 (mimid ships no UI) if it lives in its own repo or
as a test fixture rather than inside mimid.

WHAT PARLOR DOES NOT SOLVE: groups. It is one host and a queue of
visitors, one call at a time, so it never needs a group key and never
faces the problem draft-atwood-mimi-calls exists for. The MLS work is
exactly where Parlor stops.

DECISION FOR MARK: whether signalling goes before keying in the build
order, and whether the SDP-in-§5.10 mapping goes into
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi §Calls, which currently says we map no
session description at all.
